title: Dietary folate from vegetables and citrus fruit decreases plasma homocysteine concentrations in humans in a dietary controlled trial
authors: Brouwer IA, van Dusseldorp M, West CE, Meyboom S, Thomas CM, Duran M, et al.
population: Healthy adults aged 18 to 45 years in the Netherlands on fully controlled diets: high in vegetables and citrus fruit (about 560 µg folate) with placebo, low-folate diet (about 210 µg) with 250 µg/day folic acid, or low-folate diet with placebo
funder: This work was supported by the Zorg Onderzoek Nederland/Dutch Prevention Fund (28-2559), The Hague, and Unilever Research Vlaardingen.
inKindSupport: Tablets were supplied by Pharmachemie BV, Haarlem; Abbott Diagnostics provided the IMx diagnostic kits.
result: Results read from the published abstract. After 4 weeks folate status improved and homocysteine fell with both the dietary folate and the folic acid diets against placebo. From the additional 350 µg/day food folate and 250 µg/day folic acid, the bioavailability of dietary folate relative to folic acid was calculated as 60% to 98%, depending on the endpoint.
